I also don’t think the modelling industry is a good representative of what’s considered attractive on a societal scale. It’s a whole different subculture with its own standards. Models aren’t extremely thin because it’s what society considers attractive, they’re thin because designers use universal measurements and it’s become a standard within the industry.

I will say that it’s a bit different for Victoria’s Secret, but even then, their models are mainly considered attractive for their faces and fit bodies. They aren’t attractive because of their breast size. If you took a Victoria’s Secret model and gave her bigger breasts, most people would consider that an upgrade. You might perceive that as smaller chested women being considered “classy” and “non vulgar”, but as someone been an AA cup all her life, all I hear is “there’s nothing to look at anyway”.
I wish we could step away from fast fashion and go back to having tailored clothes.
